prompt: Use a loop with % and / to reverse the digits of an int, keeping the sign for negatives. Complete the reverseDigits method in the starter file, then run the tests.
explanation: The remainder operator n % 10 extracts the last decimal digit, and integer division n / 10 drops it. Each loop pass multiplies the running result by 10 and adds the extracted digit, which builds the number back up in reverse order. Handling the sign separately (remember it, work on the absolute value, reapply at the end) keeps the digit arithmetic simple.
hints: n % 10 gives the last digit of a non-negative n, and n / 10 removes it.
Keep a running result: reversed = reversed * 10 + digit on every pass, looping while the remaining value is greater than 0.
For negatives, record the sign first, reverse Math.abs(n), then negate the result before returning.
